title: New Zealand Inflation Eases in Q3
body: New Zealand's annual inflation rate eased to 3.7% in the third quarter of 2026, down from 4.1% in the previous quarter and slightly below market expectations of 3.8%. Despite this moderation, inflation remains above the Reserve Bank of New Zealand's 1–3% target range. Petrol was the single largest contributor to annual inflation, surging 19.1% amid higher international oil and fuel prices linked to conflict in the Middle East. The cost of building new homes rose 3.2%, reflecting increased material, subcontractor, labour, and fuel costs. These rates, which are measured annually in the September quarter, have been a significant driver of inflation in recent years. On a quarterly basis, the Consumer Price Index (CPI) rose 0.7%, a marked slowdown from the 1.5% increase recorded in the second quarter. title: PBOC is expected to set the USD/CNY reference rate at 6.6756 – Reuters estimate
body: The People's Bank of China is due to set the daily USD/CNY reference rate at around 0115 GMT (2115 US Eastern time), a fixing that remains one of the most closely watched signals in Asian foreign exchange markets. China operates a managed floating exchange rate system, under which the renminbi (yuan) is allowed to trade within a prescribed band around a central reference rate, or midpoint, set each trading day by the PBOC. The current trading band permits the currency to move plus or minus 2% from the official midpoint during onshore trading hours. Each morning, the PBOC determines the midpoint based on a range of inputs. These include the previous day's closing price, movements in major currencies, particularly the US dollar, broader international FX conditions, and domestic economic considerations such as capital flows, growth momentum and financial stability objectives. The midpoint is not a purely mechanical calculation, allowing policymakers discretion to guide market expectations. Once the midpoint is announced, onshore USD/CNY is free to trade within the allowable band. If market pressures push the yuan toward either edge of that range, the central bank may step in to smooth volatility. Intervention can take the form of direct buying or selling of yuan, adjustments to liquidity conditions, or guidance through state-owned banks. As a result, the daily fixing is often interpreted as a policy signal rather than just a technical reference point.

But what is driving that? Well, it's the thing we have been talking about every so often in the past two weeks, that being France's fiscal plight. And the worries are now growing rather quickly as French 10-year government bond yields have surged above 5%, hitting their highest levels since 2002. Besides that, the France-Germany 10-year yield spread is now widening towards a staggering 170 bps - its highest since 2011. It wasn't just too long ago that we were talking the line in the sand at 150 bps. All of a sudden, we're now nearly 20 bps up from that. The latest surge is another sign that investors are demanding a much higher premium to hold French debt, amid growing fiscal and political uncertainty. Looking at the EUR/CHF chart, we're already seeing some of those worries translate into price action. After all, France is Europe's second-largest economy and concerns there will have the potential to spill over into broader European assets and the euro.

title: France business confidence improves in October but cracks remain beneath the surface

This marks a slight acceleration from August 2026, when retail sales rose 6.4% compared with the same month a year earlier. Both figures are calculated on a year-over-year basis, meaning September's 6.7% reading reflects the change versus September 2025, while August's 6.4% compares to August 2025. The uptick suggests a gradual strengthening in consumer activity as the third quarter progressed, indicating that household spending continued to expand rather than lose steam heading into the autumn period. The back-to-back positive readings highlight a retail environment that remains in growth territory, with September's improvement hinting at a potentially firmer demand backdrop for Polish retailers in the closing months of 2026. Investors and policymakers will be watching upcoming data closely to see whether this upward trend in consumption proves sustainable.
